title: Scripture and Restoration
definition: Scripture and restoration belong together because God's Word calls the fallen to repentance, offers hope in grace, and guides renewed obedience.
summary: Restoration is not pretending failure never happened; it is returning to God through truth, mercy, discipline, and faith.
christFocus: Christ restores broken sinners by grace and leads them into renewed life through His Word and Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture and Restoration teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to scripture and restoration by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
